boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary
boards.description: Ten documented late-hour food destinations in New Orleans, selected as under-21-safe restaurant stops rather than nightlife venues.

cards.title: Melba's Po Boys on Elysian Fields
cards.subtitle: 1525 Elysian Fields Ave, New Orleans, LA 70117
cards.notes: Plan this as an all-hours food option, then check the restaurant’s current notices before setting out for a very late pickup.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour po-boy shop on Elysian Fields Avenue.
cards.evidence_claim: Melba’s official locations page lists the Elysian Fields restaurant at 1525 Elysian Fields Ave and lists hours of 12:00 AM–12:00 AM every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists 24-hour service daily.

cards.title: Melba's Po Boys on Tulane Avenue
cards.subtitle: 3219 Tulane Ave, New Orleans, LA 70119
cards.notes: Use the separate Tulane Avenue location when its address fits your route; confirm any holiday or weather-related update directly first.
cards.short_summary: Melba’s second New Orleans location is also listed as open around the clock.
cards.evidence_claim: Melba’s official locations page lists Melba's Tulane Ave. at 3219 Tulane Ave and says it opens 24 hours, seven days a week.
cards.access_notes: Official location page states the Tulane Avenue location opens 24 hours, seven days a week.

cards.title: McDonald's on North Broad
cards.subtitle: 1918 N Broad St, New Orleans, LA 70119
cards.notes: The lobby has earlier hours, so use the official listing to plan for the documented all-night drive-thru service rather than indoor seating.
cards.short_summary: A North Broad McDonald's with a 24-hour drive-thru listing.
cards.evidence_claim: McDonald’s official location page lists 1918 N Broad St and shows its drive-thru as open 24 hours daily; the lobby is listed until 11:00 PM.
cards.source_title: McDonald's — 1918 N Broad St, New Orleans
cards.access_notes: Drive-thru is officially listed as open 24 hours daily; lobby hours are 6:00 AM–11:00 PM.

cards.title: IHOP on Canal Street
cards.subtitle: 833 Canal St, New Orleans, LA 70112
cards.notes: Choose this full-service option when you need a sit-down stop after midnight; the official page lists its hours for every day of the week.
cards.short_summary: An IHOP on Canal Street with 24-hour daily hours.
cards.evidence_claim: IHOP’s official restaurant page for 833 Canal St lists the restaurant as open 24 hours Monday through Sunday.
cards.access_notes: Official restaurant page lists the location open 24 hours every day.

cards.title: Dat Dog Frenchmen
cards.subtitle: 601 Frenchmen St, New Orleans, LA 70116
cards.notes: For a late meal, use the published Friday–Saturday closing time and verify the day’s schedule before traveling across town.
cards.short_summary: A Frenchmen Street restaurant listed until 3:00 AM on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.evidence_claim: Dat Dog’s official locations page lists Dat Dog Frenchmen at 601 Frenchmen St, open until 3:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours: midnight Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: U Pizza on Saint Charles
cards.subtitle: 1513 Saint Charles Ave, New Orleans, LA 70130
cards.notes: Use the restaurant’s Friday–Saturday 2:00 AM listing for a late pizza pickup, and check its posted hours again before departure.
cards.short_summary: A Saint Charles Avenue pizza restaurant with 2:00 AM weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: U Pizza’s official website lists 1513 Saint Charles Ave and business and carryout hours until 2:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list midnight Sunday–Thursday and 2:00 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: 13 on Frenchmen Street
cards.subtitle: 517 Frenchmen St, New Orleans, LA 70116
cards.notes: Target the listed Friday-through-Sunday late window for food, and consult the restaurant’s own page for any last-minute operating changes.
cards.short_summary: A Frenchmen Street food stop listed until 4:00 AM Friday through Sunday.
cards.evidence_claim: 13 on Frenchmen Street’s official menu page lists 517 Frenchmen St and hours until 4:00 AM on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.
cards.source_title: 13 on Frenchmen Street — Menu and Hours
cards.access_notes: Official hours list 4:00 AM Friday–Sunday, 1:00 AM Tuesday–Thursday; no Monday hours are listed.

cards.title: New York Pizza
cards.subtitle: New Orleans, LA
cards.notes: Use the official restaurant-hours listing when planning a weeknight late pickup, and verify the exact location and service mode before going.
cards.short_summary: A New Orleans pizza restaurant with 2:00 AM Monday hours listed.
cards.evidence_claim: New York Pizza’s official website lists restaurant hours of 5:00 PM–2:00 AM on Monday.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists Monday restaurant hours until 2:00 AM; check the site for the applicable day.

cards.title: Magazine Pizza
cards.subtitle: 1068 Magazine St, New Orleans, LA 70130
cards.notes: Plan a Friday or Saturday order around the restaurant’s published 2:00 AM close, checking directly if an event changes normal service.
cards.short_summary: A Magazine Street pizza restaurant listed until 2:00 AM on Friday and Saturday.
cards.evidence_claim: Magazine Pizza’s official website lists 1068 Magazine Street and Friday–Saturday hours of 11:00 AM–2:00 AM.
cards.access_notes: Official hours list midnight Sunday–Thursday and 2:00 AM Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Dat Dog Frenchmen Late Stop
cards.subtitle: 601 Frenchmen St, New Orleans, LA 70116
cards.notes: Use published weekend late hours and check official updates before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Frenchmen Street food destination with late weekend hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Dat Dog Frenchmen is listed open until 3:00 AM Friday and Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Friday–Saturday hours until 3:00 AM.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named NOBTS campus destinations documented by current institutional dining, chapel, orientation, handbook, and campus-guide sources.

cards.title: Leavell Chapel
cards.subtitle: Campus worship and semester gatherings
cards.notes: Check the chapel calendar before you go, then join an in-person Tuesday or Thursday service during the semester at 11 a.m.
cards.short_summary: The seminary’s scheduled chapel gathering place.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS invites people to chapel services on Tuesdays and Thursdays during the semester at 11:00 a.m.; its orientation schedule places worship and welcome in Leavell Chapel.
cards.source_title: Welcome to NOBTS and Leavell College Chapel
cards.access_notes: Service schedule is semester-specific; verify the current chapel calendar before visiting.

cards.title: John T. Christian Library
cards.subtitle: Map-listed academic resource
cards.notes: Use the library as a named study stop; check its services and access details with NOBTS before planning a longer research session.
cards.short_summary: A campus-map-listed library destination for academic work.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s campus guide identifies the John T. Christian Library as an academic building on the New Orleans campus.
cards.access_notes: Confirm visitor and borrowing access directly with the library.

cards.title: Luter Student Center
cards.subtitle: Student-center atrium and campus offices
cards.notes: Start in the atrium to orient yourself, then ask Student Life about current campus activities or use the listed student services.
cards.short_summary: The orientation venue for campus expos, games, and student support.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s Spring 2026 orientation schedules a campus expo, NOLA Expo, and game night in the Luter Student Center atrium, and directs students there for help.
cards.access_notes: Activities and offices vary by term; check current Student Life information.

cards.title: Cafe New Orleans
cards.subtitle: Inside the Luter Student Center
cards.notes: Use this Luter Student Center coffee-and-light-breakfast stop on a weekday, but check the day’s hours and chapel closure before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Campus café serving coffee, drinks, and light breakfast items.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that Cafe New Orleans is in the Luter Student Center and offers coffee, drinks, and light breakfast items on weekday mornings.
cards.access_notes: NOBTS lists opening at 7:30 a.m. on weekdays, varying evening hours, and Tuesday/Thursday chapel closures.

cards.title: Landrum Leavell Dining Hall
cards.subtitle: Main NOBTS cafeteria
cards.notes: Plan a weekday breakfast or lunch here when classes are in session; current offerings and any guest arrangements should be confirmed with dining.
cards.short_summary: The seminary’s main cafeteria and an orientation meal venue.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS identifies Landrum Leavell Dining Hall as its main cafeteria and lists breakfast and lunch for purchase Monday through Friday when classes are in session.
cards.access_notes: Service is tied to classes being in session; meals require purchase unless an event provides them.

cards.title: Martin Chapel
cards.subtitle: Named campus chapel venue
cards.notes: Look for scheduled programs before visiting; the 2026 orientation used Martin Chapel for a THRIVE-hosted date-night event for married couples.
cards.short_summary: A second named chapel venue used for scheduled campus programming.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s Spring 2026 orientation schedule places a THRIVE-hosted Date Night in Martin Chapel, and the campus guide lists Martin Chapel.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled events; the cited event was specifically for married couples.

cards.title: Bunyan Building
cards.subtitle: Classroom building
cards.notes: Use posted room locations to find classes or academic sessions; orientation assigned multiple graduate-program breakouts to Bunyan rooms.
cards.short_summary: A campus classroom building used for program sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s Spring 2026 orientation scheduled breakout and degree-program sessions in Bunyan Building rooms 101–108.
cards.access_notes: Classrooms may be occupied or access-controlled outside scheduled sessions.

cards.title: REC Center
cards.subtitle: Campus recreation facility
cards.notes: Ask Student Life or the recreation coordinator about current recreation programming and facility access before making plans to use the center.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation destination in the NOBTS campus guide.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s campus guide lists the REC Center among campus housing and facilities, and the Student Handbook identifies a recreation coordinator in Student Life.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current facility hours, eligibility, and activity availability with Student Life.

cards.entity_name: Doris Kelley Showers of Blessings Building
cards.title: Campus Common Goods
cards.subtitle: Doris Kelley Showers of Blessings Building
cards.notes: Eligible on-campus students can check the current pantry windows and contact Student Life if they need grocery staples, household goods, or guidance.
cards.short_summary: The on-campus location of the Campus Common Goods resource.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2026–27 NOBTS Student Handbook says Campus Common Goods serves on-campus students from the Doris Kelley Showers of Blessings Building and lists pantry items and hours.
cards.source_title: NOBTS and Leavell College Student Handbook, 2026–27
cards.access_notes: For on-campus NOBTS and Leavell College students; handbook lists Monday 9–11 a.m. and Wednesday 4–6 p.m.

cards.title: Legacy Plaza
cards.subtitle: In front of Leavell Chapel
cards.notes: Walk through the plaza before or after a scheduled chapel event and read the commemorative bricks and pavers without treating the space as a drop-in venue.
cards.short_summary: A chapel-front plaza marked by commemorative bricks and a bronze seal.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that Legacy Plaza is in front of Leavell Chapel and receives Legacy Brick installations; premium pavers are placed beside its bronze seal.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; follow campus access and event guidance.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase activities at New Orleans Public Library spaces, with no library card needed for the puzzle exchanges or REACH Center workspace.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Algiers Regional Library
cards.title: Trade puzzles at Algiers Regional Library
cards.subtitle: Algiers Regional Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Stop by the Community Puzzle Exchange, choose a puzzle to take, and return it when you finish; a library card and formal checkout are not required.
cards.short_summary: A take-one, return-when-ready puzzle activity.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Algiers Regional Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; exchange items are not formally checked out and are not moderated by library staff.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Alvar Library
cards.title: Pick out a puzzle at Alvar Library
cards.subtitle: Alvar Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Browse the Community Puzzle Exchange with a friend, take a puzzle even if you have none to trade, then bring it back after completing it.
cards.short_summary: A low-key puzzle swap with no checkout desk step.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Alvar Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; you may take a puzzle without leaving one, then return it when done.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Central City Library
cards.title: Start a shared puzzle from Central City
cards.subtitle: Central City Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Choose a puzzle from the exchange for an unplugged hang, work on it together off-site, and return the box to keep the exchange circulating.
cards.short_summary: Borrow a jigsaw without a card or checkout.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Central City Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; exchange items are not formally checked out and are not moderated by library staff.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Cita Dennis Hubbell Library
cards.title: Browse puzzles at Cita Dennis Hubbell
cards.subtitle: Cita Dennis Hubbell Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Make a quick puzzle-picking stop, take one from the community shelf, and plan a relaxed group session before returning it after you are finished.
cards.short_summary: An informal puzzle exchange for all skill levels.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Cita Dennis Hubbell Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; a puzzle may be taken without contributing one first.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at East New Orleans Regional Library
cards.title: Find a puzzle at East New Orleans Regional
cards.subtitle: East New Orleans Regional Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Use the exchange as the start of a screen-free hang: select a box, set up a shared build, and return the puzzle afterward for another visitor.
cards.short_summary: A free puzzle activity housed in a regional library.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists East New Orleans Regional Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; exchange items are free and have no official checkout process.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Mid-City Library
cards.title: Take a puzzle from Mid-City Library
cards.subtitle: Mid-City Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Look through the community puzzle shelf, choose a box for a quiet afternoon, and return it when complete so the next person can use it.
cards.short_summary: A card-free puzzle borrow-and-return activity.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Mid-City Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; you can take a puzzle without a library card or formal checkout.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Milton H. Latter Memorial Library
cards.title: Set up a puzzle hang from Latter Library
cards.subtitle: Milton H. Latter Memorial Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Choose a community puzzle for a cooperative activity, keep the pieces together, and bring it back when you are done rather than checking it out.
cards.short_summary: A shared project sourced from the library’s exchange shelf.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Milton H. Latter Memorial Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; the exchange operates without an official checkout process.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Robert E. Smith Library
cards.title: Choose a jigsaw at Robert E. Smith
cards.subtitle: Robert E. Smith Library, New Orleans
cards.notes: Drop in to select a puzzle from the exchange, make it a shared table project, and return the box after completion for another community member.
cards.short_summary: A no-card puzzle exchange at a named library branch.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Robert E. Smith Library as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; items can be taken and returned without a library card.

cards.entity_name: Community Puzzle Exchange at Rosa F. Keller Library and Community Center
cards.title: Swap a puzzle at Rosa F. Keller
cards.subtitle: Rosa F. Keller Library and Community Center, New Orleans
cards.notes: Browse the puzzle exchange for a ready-made group activity, take a box without a checkout, and return it when your group has finished the build.
cards.short_summary: An easy, equipment-free group activity from a community shelf.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library lists Rosa F. Keller Library and Community Center as a Community Puzzle Exchange location and says participants do not need a library card or an official checkout process.
cards.source_title: New Year, New Hobbies – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Use during the library’s open hours; a library card is not needed and no official checkout is used.

cards.title: Work together at the REACH Center
cards.subtitle: Corpus Christi-Epiphany Community Resource Center, 2022 St. Bernard Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a project or reading, claim time in the free coworking space, and visit the public art gallery; the center says everyone is welcome without a library card.
cards.short_summary: A free coworking and public-art space in the Seventh Ward.
cards.evidence_claim: The New Orleans Public Library describes the REACH Center as a free coworking space and public art gallery, and states that a library card is not needed to use the space.
cards.source_title: REACH Center – New Orleans Public Library
cards.access_notes: Staffed Tuesday through Thursday, 10 a.m.–2 p.m.; Monday and Friday are by appointment only. Closed Saturday and Sunday.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented academic work settings on the New Orleans campus, centered on library collections, research tools, computers, and writing support.

cards.title: Reference Room
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library
cards.notes: Bring a defined research question, then use the reference books, theses, and computer resources gathered in this study-and-research room.
cards.short_summary: A library room expressly equipped for study and research alongside reference materials and theses.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that reference books, theses, and computer resources are in the Reference Room, where facilities are provided for study and research.
cards.source_title: About the John T. Christian Library
cards.access_notes: Ask at the circulation desk for information about library materials; the source does not publish room hours or reservation rules.

cards.title: Martin Music Library
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use this specialized collection when your assignment involves music or worship; confirm material availability with library staff before planning a visit.
cards.short_summary: A specialized campus library for music and worship resources.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS identifies the Martin Music Library as a specialized library with extensive music and worship resources and lists it on the second floor of its main campus libraries.
cards.access_notes: The source lists the library’s location but does not publish current hours or seating rules.

cards.title: Curriculum Lab
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Start with the catalog or circulation desk, then use the designated Curriculum Lab when you need curriculum-oriented print resources.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor library area for curriculum-focused resource work.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s library location guide lists the Curriculum Lab among the physical resources on the second floor.
cards.access_notes: The source confirms the location but gives no current public access, hours, or reservation details.

cards.title: Course Reserves
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Check your course reading list and catalog status first, then work from the library’s designated Course Reserves area for assigned materials.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library area dedicated to course-reserve materials.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s library location guide lists Course Reserves on the second floor of its main campus libraries.
cards.access_notes: Confirm an item’s status in the online catalog; the source does not publish current reserve-use rules.

cards.title: Periodicals
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the periodicals area for journal-led reading; identify the title in the catalog before heading upstairs to locate the physical issue.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor area for working with the library’s periodicals collection.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s library location guide lists Periodicals on the second floor and directs users to review location and status in the catalog.
cards.access_notes: Use the catalog to verify an item’s physical location and availability; public hours are not provided on this page.

cards.title: Microforms & Microform Reader
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Plan a focused source-review session here when your research requires microform materials, and ask library staff for current equipment guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named second-floor library area with microforms and a microform reader.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS lists Microforms and a Microform Reader among the physical resources on the second floor of its main campus libraries.
cards.access_notes: The source confirms the resource and location but does not state current equipment availability or assistance hours.

cards.title: Book Stacks A–BT
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Use the call number from the catalog to browse this A–BT run, which includes philosophy, religion, Christian history, biblical studies, and theology.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor open-stack research zone covering call numbers A through BT.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS lists Book Stacks A–BT on the second floor and identifies subject ranges there including philosophy, religion, Christian history, biblical studies, and theology.
cards.access_notes: The library says its book stacks are open for students and other patrons to select books; verify individual item status in the catalog.

cards.title: Book Stacks BT–Z
cards.subtitle: John T. Christian Library, second floor
cards.notes: Follow the catalog call number into the BT–Z stacks for theology, ministry, history, education, music, languages, and related subjects.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor open-stack research zone covering call numbers BT through Z.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS lists Book Stacks BT–Z on the second floor and identifies ranges there including pastoral ministries, missions, education, music, languages, and medicine.
cards.access_notes: The library says its book stacks are open for students and other patrons to select books; verify individual item status in the catalog.

cards.title: Information Technology Center (ITC)
cards.subtitle: Hardin Student Center, second floor
cards.notes: Use an available desktop computer for course work or research, and contact ITC support if you need help with campus technology services.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor Hardin Student Center computer workspace for students.
cards.evidence_claim: An NOBTS course document states that desktop computers are available for student use in the Information Technology Center on the second floor of the Hardin Student Center.
cards.access_notes: The current official campus guide lists ITC hours as Monday–Friday, 7 a.m.–10 p.m.; desktop computers are described as available to students.

cards.title: Writing Center
cards.subtitle: Hardin Student Center, room 290B
cards.notes: Bring a draft or assignment requirements and use the center’s writing guidance; check its official page for current appointment information before arriving.
cards.short_summary: A Hardin Student Center writing-support location with academic-paper guidance.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that its Writing Center is located in the Hardin Student Center, room 290B, and provides guides, tips, and information for academic papers and essays.
cards.access_notes: The cited NOBTS document says appointment information is available through the Writing Center page; it does not state current public hours.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations on practical Gentilly and lakefront corridors from the seminary campus, with one documented reason to seek each out.

cards.title: See a neighboring university campus
cards.subtitle: Gentilly Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Walk the Gentilly Boulevard edge and use Dillard’s visitor information to plan a weekday campus visit or an admissions tour.
cards.short_summary: A nearby university with scheduled visitor access.
cards.evidence_claim: Dillard University lists its address at 2601 Gentilly Boulevard and says campus visits and tours are available by appointment.
cards.access_notes: Visitor tours require an appointment; see Dillard’s visit page for current scheduling and closure details.

cards.title: Locate a public-library branch
cards.subtitle: Gentilly Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Bring a reading list or a device and check the branch’s current calendar and hours before heading to 3001 Gentilly Boulevard.
cards.short_summary: A named New Orleans Public Library branch in Gentilly.
cards.evidence_claim: New Orleans Public Library identifies Norman Mayer Library at 3001 Gentilly Boulevard, New Orleans.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library’s live listing for current hours and services.

cards.title: Spot a long-running Gentilly school
cards.subtitle: Elysian Fields Avenue corridor
cards.notes: Use Elysian Fields Avenue to identify Brother Martin’s campus, then rely on the school for any public-event or visitor details.
cards.short_summary: A named secondary-school campus on Elysian Fields.

cards.title: Check the recreation-center schedule

cards.notes: Look for NORD programming at Milne and confirm registration, age range, and session details before making the Franklin Avenue trip.
cards.short_summary: A city recreation-center destination on Franklin Avenue.

cards.title: Find SUNO’s campus corridor

cards.notes: Use the SUNO contact page to orient to the campus and its weekday office hours before arranging any campus-related errand.

cards.title: Head toward the Lakefront campus

cards.access_notes: Check UNO’s visitor and building-access guidance before entering campus facilities.

cards.title: Check the arena calendar

cards.notes: Use the venue’s event listing to see what is scheduled at Lakefront Arena, then choose a ticketed or public event that fits your plans.

cards.source_title: Lakefront Arena Events and Venue Details
cards.access_notes: Entry and ticket requirements depend on the individual event.

cards.title: See the lakefront airport terminal
cards.subtitle: Stars and Stripes Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Use the airport’s contact information to identify the terminal and check its visitor guidance before making a daytime aviation-focused stop.
cards.short_summary: A named lakefront airport terminal with public contact information.

cards.title: Use a major city park address

cards.notes: Plan a daylight park visit around the Read Boulevard entrance and check city recreation notices for any facility-specific programming.
cards.short_summary: A city-listed park destination in eastern Gentilly.

cards.source_title: City of New Orleans Parks and Greenspace by Jurisdiction
cards.access_notes: Outdoor access and recreation programming can change with weather and city operations.

cards.title: Find a city playground site
cards.subtitle: Lapeyrouse Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the named playground as a neighborhood recreation waypoint and check NORD materials for current activities or facility access before going.
cards.short_summary: A city-documented playground site in Gentilly.
cards.evidence_claim: A New Orleans City Council record identifies Stallings-Gentilly Playground at 2700 Lapeyrouse Street, New Orleans.
cards.access_notes: Verify current NORD programming and site conditions before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten recurring NOBTS gatherings and practices documented by current seminary calendars, chapel, student-life, and news sources.

cards.title: Marking the Seminary’s Beginning
cards.subtitle: Annual October chapel observance
cards.notes: Plan around the October chapel gathering, which recognizes the seminary’s founding and its continuing institutional story.
cards.short_summary: An October chapel tradition tied to NOBTS’s founding.
cards.evidence_claim: The 2026–27 Graduate Program Calendar schedules Founders’ Day Chapel for October 6, 2026; NOBTS describes Founders’ Day as an October observance of the school’s October 1, 1917 opening.
cards.access_notes: See the current Graduate Program Calendar and chapel schedule for the annual date and attendance details.

cards.title: Opening the Semester Together
cards.subtitle: Leavell Chapel academic-year opening
cards.notes: Attend the opening Convocation in Leavell Chapel to see the seminary formally begin a new semester and welcome students.
cards.short_summary: The formal chapel service that launches each semester.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS reported that its January 2026 Convocation officially kicked off the spring semester, and its August 2025 Convocation marked the official start of the academic year.
cards.source_title: NOBTS kicks off spring semester with Convocation service
cards.access_notes: Scheduled at the start of each semester; confirm the date on the current chapel calendar.

cards.title: The Tuesday-and-Thursday Chapel Rhythm
cards.subtitle: Leavell Chapel during the semester
cards.notes: Build your visit around the regular 11 a.m. chapel rhythm, held twice weekly during the semester and available online.
cards.short_summary: A standing twice-weekly worship gathering for the campus community.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that chapel services are held Tuesdays and Thursdays during the semester at 11:00 a.m. and can also be joined online.
cards.source_title: Welcome to NOBTS and Leavell College Chapel
cards.access_notes: Held Tuesdays and Thursdays at 11 a.m. during the semester; check the chapel page for speakers and changes.

cards.title: Classes Pause for Serve Day
cards.subtitle: Once-a-semester community service practice
cards.notes: Join a service team after chapel when scheduled; the day pairs local projects with a campus debrief afterward.
cards.short_summary: A semesterly day of campus-organized service across New Orleans.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS calls Serve Day a once-a-semester event; in February 2026, participants served in 22 groups after chapel and gathered afterward for a debrief.
cards.source_title: More than 250 participate in NOBTS Serve Day
cards.access_notes: Participation and project locations vary; use the Spiritual Formation and Student Life page for the current sign-up.

cards.title: A Week Set Aside for Missions
cards.subtitle: Annual Global Mission Center emphasis
cards.notes: Watch for the spring schedule of chapel guests, a missions expo, prayer opportunities, and conversations with mission partners.
cards.short_summary: An annual week connecting the campus with missionaries and mission opportunities.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS says it highlights missions during Missions Week every year; the 2026 week included guest speakers, a missions expo, prayer room, lunch, and chapel events.
cards.source_title: Missions Week offers opportunity to connect with IMB missionaries
cards.access_notes: The event is held in spring; consult NOBTS news and the chapel schedule for current activities.

cards.title: Defend, Seventeen Years In
cards.subtitle: Annual NOBTS apologetics conference
cards.notes: Follow the conference schedule for lectures and breakout sessions focused on Christian apologetics and related questions.
cards.short_summary: A long-running annual apologetics gathering at NOBTS.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS hosted the 17th annual Defend Apologetics Conference on January 4–9, 2026, with plenary lectures and breakout sessions.
cards.access_notes: Held annually; registration, eligibility, and session details are announced with each conference.

cards.title: Abide’s Annual Campus Weekend
cards.subtitle: NOBTS Prepare Her conference
cards.notes: If eligible, look for the winter conference’s plenary worship and breakout sessions hosted by the NOBTS Prepare Her team.
cards.short_summary: A recurring NOBTS-hosted women’s conference begun in 2021.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS described its January 2026 Abide Women’s Conference as the fifth annual event and said the conference began in 2021.
cards.source_title: Sold-out Abide Women’s Conference focuses on worship
cards.access_notes: This is a women’s conference; consult the Abide event information for registration and current access details.

cards.title: The Prepare Here Pastor’s Summit
cards.subtitle: Jim Henry Leadership Institute annual conference
cards.notes: Track the fall summit if you are a senior pastor or partner participant; its program centers on leadership-focused plenaries and breakouts.
cards.short_summary: An annual NOBTS leadership conference for senior pastors.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jim Henry Leadership Institute identifies the Prepare Here Pastor’s Summit as its annual leadership conference and reports its third annual conference was held at NOBTS in October 2025.
cards.source_title: Jim Henry Leadership Institute 2026 Impact Report
cards.access_notes: Intended for senior pastors and partner conventions; review the current summit announcement for participation requirements.

cards.title: Closing the Year with Recognition
cards.subtitle: Annual NOBTS chapel service
cards.notes: Catch the final spring chapel recognition service, where NOBTS highlights student, faculty, staff, and institutional achievements.
cards.short_summary: An annual end-of-spring chapel ceremony recognizing the NOBTS community.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS reports that the annual Celebration of Excellence service honors notable student performance and faculty achievement; the 2026 service was held May 5.
cards.source_title: Students commissioned, honored during NOBTS chapel services
cards.access_notes: Held near the close of spring classes; verify the current chapel calendar for the service date.

cards.title: Degrees Conferred in Worship
cards.subtitle: NOBTS and Leavell College commencement
cards.notes: Attend commencement to see degrees conferred within a worship service that includes Scripture and a ministry-focused charge.
cards.short_summary: A commencement format NOBTS explicitly describes as a worship service.
cards.evidence_claim: At fall 2025 commencement, NOBTS President Jamie Dew described the ceremony as a worship service in which degrees are also conferred.
cards.source_title: NOBTS celebrates more than 250 fall graduates
cards.access_notes: Commencement dates and guest procedures vary by term; consult the Registrar’s current graduation information.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A calm first-weekend sequence for getting oriented to named campus destinations, finding study and gathering points, and checking current access details in person.

cards.entity_name: New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary Campus Map
cards.title: Start with the campus map
cards.subtitle: Orientation stop • 3939 Gentilly Blvd.
cards.notes: Open the official map before setting out, then use it to identify the Luter Student Center, library, chapel, and dining locations.
cards.short_summary: Use the official map to turn an unfamiliar campus into a short, walkable plan.
cards.evidence_claim: The NOBTS catalog provides an official campus map.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary Catalog
cards.access_notes: Consult the map and campus offices for current building access and event information.

cards.title: Find the Luter Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus orientation stop
cards.notes: Locate the student center early so you know where Café New Orleans, campus police, student-life contacts, and other listed services are based.
cards.short_summary: A practical reference point for several student-facing campus services.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s directory lists Café New Orleans, Campus Police, and Leavell College offices at LSC locations.
cards.access_notes: Check the directory or student services for current office availability.

cards.title: Check in at Café New Orleans
cards.subtitle: Luter Student Center • weekday café
cards.notes: Use the café as a simple daytime meeting point, and confirm its current hours before relying on it for coffee or a light breakfast.
cards.short_summary: A campus café serving coffee, drinks, and light breakfast items.
cards.evidence_claim: Café New Orleans is in the Luter Student Center and offers coffee, drinks, and light breakfast items on weekday mornings.
cards.access_notes: The seminary says weekday hours vary and the café closes for Tuesday and Thursday chapel services; verify before visiting.

cards.title: Locate the main dining hall
cards.subtitle: Campus meal-planning stop
cards.notes: Find the dining hall on your first pass through campus, then ask dining staff about the current service schedule and payment options.
cards.short_summary: The seminary identifies this as its main cafeteria.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS identifies Landrum Leavell Dining Hall as its main cafeteria, with meals available for purchase Monday through Friday when classes are in session.
cards.access_notes: Service is described as Monday–Friday when classes are in session; confirm the current schedule before going.

cards.title: Make the library your study anchor
cards.subtitle: Campus study stop
cards.notes: Walk to the library, note the circulation desk, and practice locating one catalog item by its collection, call number, and status.
cards.short_summary: A two-floor library with stacks, reference material, course reserves, and specialized collections.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS explains that its main-campus library has physical collections on two floors and provides instructions for locating catalog items.
cards.source_title: NOBTS Library: Locating Items, Guides, and Helps
cards.access_notes: Some archives and rare collections are listed as restricted; ask at the circulation desk about access.

cards.title: Spot Leavell Chapel for the week ahead
cards.subtitle: Campus gathering-place stop
cards.notes: Locate the chapel while you are already walking the central campus, then check student communications for the next chapel service or program.
cards.short_summary: A named campus chapel shown on the official NOBTS campus map.
cards.evidence_claim: The official NOBTS campus map lists Leavell Chapel as a campus facility.
cards.source_title: Campus Map | New Orleans Baptist Theological Seminary Catalog
cards.access_notes: Event schedules and building access may change; confirm details through current seminary communications.

cards.title: Ask about the Bible Museum
cards.subtitle: Luter Student Center • collection stop
cards.notes: Add the museum to your orientation loop and contact the listed museum office to learn whether a visit or program is available that weekend.
cards.short_summary: A named NOBTS museum contact listed at the Luter Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s directory lists the Bible Museum and identifies its location as LSC.
cards.access_notes: Confirm current visitor access, programming, and any admission terms directly with the museum.

cards.title: Pin the Caskey Center
cards.subtitle: Campus resource stop
cards.notes: Find the Caskey Center on the map and save its contact details; it is a useful named destination to recognize as you learn campus services.
cards.short_summary: A campus center listed by NOBTS with its own contact information.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS’s directory lists the Caskey Center for Church Excellence and its contact information.
cards.access_notes: Contact the center for current programs, appointments, and building access.

cards.title: Note River City Café for events
cards.subtitle: Campus dining and event-space stop
cards.notes: Locate River City Café near the dining area and keep it in mind when you see a campus event notice that names its private dining rooms.
cards.short_summary: A campus café whose private dining rooms may be scheduled for special events.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that River City Café and its private dining rooms are available for special events scheduled through the Conference Office.
cards.access_notes: Availability is tied to scheduled events; contact the Conference Office or dining staff for current access.

cards.title: Save the counseling center location
cards.subtitle: LifeSongs Building • student support stop
cards.notes: Identify the center beside the Luter Student Center and save its contact information now, so you know where to ask about confidential support later.
cards.short_summary: A campus counseling center offering confidential services and student support.
cards.evidence_claim: NOBTS states that counseling occurs at the Leeke Magee Christian Counseling Center in the LifeSongs Building next to the Luter Student Center, and services are free for NOBTS students.
cards.access_notes: Call 504-816-8004 to arrange an appointment or ask at the front desk; support is confidential.
